title: Inappropriate Virtues and Flaws for Faeries
heading: Inappropriate Virtues and Flaws
summary: Lists which Virtues and Flaws a faerie character may never take (Gift, Hermetic, Divine/Infernal powers, human social status and upbringing) and what to take instead.
quotes: Faeries may not have The Gift, or any Virtue or Flaw specific to Hermetic magi.
If the faerie has a role that makes it appear part of human society, it should take the Infiltrator Virtue.

title: Faeries and Confidence
heading: Confidence
summary: Faeries have no Confidence scores; the Reputation as Confidence Virtue gives them false Confidence points to back up their Reputations.
quotes: Faeries do not have Confidence scores.
A faerie with this Virtue gains a number of false Confidence points equal to its highest reputation

title: Faerie Personality Flaws
heading: Personality Flaws
summary: Sets how many Personality Flaws a faerie may take, noting that role-linked Flaws are often required.
quotes: Faeries may have up to three Minor Personality Flaws and one Major Personality Flaw

title: Focus Power
heading: Focus Power
summary: Virtue giving a faerie a themed, spontaneous-style power built from a pool of spell levels, with Might cost and Initiative set by the effect's magnitude.
quotes: The player receives 25 spell levels to spend on this power.
an initiative score of (the character's Quickness – the power's maximum magnitude)

title: Greater Power
heading: Greater Power
summary: Virtue giving a faerie formulaic spell-like powers designed at character creation, with a reduced Might cost and Initiative penalty compared to Lesser Powers.
quotes: Taking this Virtue gives the character 50 spell levels to spend on these powers
Each power has a Might Point cost equal to (the magnitude of the effect / 2)

title: Lesser Power
heading: Lesser Power
summary: Minor Virtue giving a faerie formulaic spell-like powers; cheaper to acquire than Greater Powers but each use costs more Might and is slower.
quotes: Taking this Virtue gives the character 25 spell levels to spend on these powers
Each effect's Might Point cost is equal to the magnitude of the effect.

title: Personal Power
heading: Personal Power
summary: Minor Virtue giving a faerie a single Personal-range spell-like power designed like a formulaic spell.
quotes: Personal powers must have Personal Range.

title: An Exemplary Catalog of Faerie Powers
heading: An Exemplary Catalog of Faerie Powers
summary: General rules for using faerie powers: spending Might for uses, Penetration, wound penalties, running out of Might, and powers across realm boundaries.
quotes: Faeries gain one use of a power each time they spend its cost in Might.
Might Score – (5 x Might Point cost) + Penetration bonus

title: Intricacy Points
heading: Intricacy Points
summary: Intricacy points let a faerie make a power faster or cheaper in Might, and can be gained from unspent spell levels or the Improved Powers Virtue.
quotes: Every 5 unspent levels equal an intricacy point.

title: Odd Targets and Durations
heading: Odd Targets and Durations
summary: Allows faerie powers to use Merinita Ranges, Targets and Durations, and defines the Until Duration and dual Durations.
quotes: In this book it is treated as being equivalent to Year, but not requiring a Ritual.

title: Faerie Power Virtue Comparison Table
heading: Faerie Power Virtue Comparison Table
summary: Table comparing spell levels, effect type, Might cost and Initiative for each faerie power Virtue.
quotes: Qik – maximum magnitude

title: Ritual Power
heading: Ritual Power
summary: Major Virtue for ritual-level faerie effects, which cost Might Score as well as Might points whenever they are used.
quotes: All Ritual Powers are at least Level 20, regardless of the actual level of the effect
The Initiative for the power is equal to the character's Quickness – (the magnitude of the effect x 2).

title: Improved Powers
heading: Improved Powers
summary: Minor Virtue granting intricacy points to a faerie's powers, or optionally mastery-like abilities for them.
quotes: This Virtue gives the character 5 intricacy points to spend on any of its powers.

title: Constant Powers
heading: Constant Powers
summary: Rules for making a Greater, Lesser or Personal Power constant, triggering at every sunrise and sunset.
quotes: costs an additional magnitude

title: Binding Oath
heading: Binding Oath
summary: Ritual faerie power enforcing solemn oaths and contracts, warning and then penalising humans who break them.
quotes: Faeries cannot break their oaths

title: Granting Virtues and Flaws
heading: Grant (Major Virtue)
summary: Ritual faerie powers that impose a Virtue or Flaw (blessing or curse) on a target, permanently at the cost of Might Score or temporarily at the cost of Might points.
quotes: The creature can decide to bestow the Virtue permanently or temporarily.

title: Craft Magical Trinket
heading: Craft Magical Trinket
summary: Faerie power that creates a glamour object letting its holder use one Virtue once, at a Might cost depending on the Virtue's size.
quotes: A trinket costs 10 Might points if it invokes a Minor Virtue, and 15 points if it invokes a Major Virtue.

title: Converting Greater Powers to Lesser Powers
heading: Conversion
summary: Quick procedure to convert a Greater Power to a Lesser Power by adjusting Might cost and Initiative.
quotes: double the Might cost and quadruple the Initiative penalty of the power

title: Greater and Lesser Faerie Powers
heading: Greater and Lesser Faerie Powers
summary: Explains how Lesser Powers compare with Greater Powers and how the powers listed in the book are presented, including the Initiative bonus.
quotes: each use costs twice as much Might as the equivalent Greater Power

title: Loosely Material
heading: Loosely Material
summary: Power letting an immaterial faerie take on a physical body, whose Characteristics and Size are bought with Might points spent on activation.
quotes: For each Might point spent on this power, 5 characteristic points are available to spend on the four physical Characteristics of Strength, Stamina, Dexterity, and Quickness.
A faerie's material body can have any Size up to a maximum of its Presence unless it spends additional Might points on Size.

title: Powers of Transformation
heading: Powers of Transformation
summary: Advice on which faerie power Virtue to use when designing transformation powers, depending on whether specific or varied substances are involved.
quotes: then that is best designed as a Greater Power

title: Focus Powers
heading: Focus Powers
summary: Intro to Focus Powers: broad themed effects whose Might cost and Initiative follow the magnitude produced, to be agreed with the troupe.
quotes: Each use of a focus power has a Might Point cost equal to the magnitude of the effect

title: Extended Glamour
heading: Extended Glamour
summary: Power letting a faerie be aware of everything in its domain, with the domain's size set by the faerie's Might Score, and yielding vis each year.
quotes: The faerie's Might score determines the size of area possible: a Room (5–10 Might), a Structure (15–25 Might), or a standard Boundary (30+ Might).
The area controlled by the faerie can produce a yearly harvest of (Might/10) pawns of vis

title: Power Design: An Example
heading: Power Design: An Example
summary: Worked example of designing faerie powers from Hermetic spells, choosing between Personal, Greater, Lesser and Focus Powers and spending intricacy points.
quotes: Personal powers cost (magnitude/2) points, rounding up

title: Pretense: Faerie Abilities
heading: Pretense: Faerie Abilities
summary: Explains that faeries use Pretenses in place of Abilities, and that few faeries can teach humans, especially those linked to the dead.
quotes: Some exceptional faeries are able to teach Abilities to humans.

title: Faerie Instructor and Faerie Trainer
heading: Faerie Instructor
requires: Virtue: Faerie Instructor or Faerie Trainer
summary: Virtues allowing a faerie to teach humans, either by trading stored Abilities or by training with conventional methods.
quotes: The faerie imparts the Ability by trading it for the Ability that the student currently has.

title: Player-Defined Pretenses
heading: Player-Defined Pretenses
summary: Pretenses tied to a faerie's story role rather than a human Ability must be negotiated with the troupe.
quotes: These player-defined pretenses must be negotiated with the troupe.

title: Resistance and Pretenses
heading: Resistance and Pretenses
summary: Explains that Pretenses guide a faerie's own actions and so are not resisted by Parma Magica, unlike powers or tools aimed at a magus.
quotes: they are not resisted by Parma Magica

title: Player-Defined Pretense Example: Chivalrous Combat
heading: Player-Defined Pretense Example: Chivalrous Combat
summary: Worked example of negotiating a broad player-defined Pretense with a built-in limitation.

title: Increasing Pretense
heading: Increasing Pretense
summary: How faeries gain Pretense experience by closely involving themselves in humans' stories each season, plus the Virtues and Flaws that change how often this occurs.
quotes: Faeries cannot gain experience from study, training, or practice
During character creation an ostentatious faerie has a Pretense multiplier of 25 instead of 15.

title: Faerie Advancement Through Change
heading: Faerie Advancement Through Change
summary: Overview of what a faerie needs to alter its role and gain powers: cognizance, stored Pretense points, and a creative human collaborator.
quotes: It requires the potential to change within its glamour, represented by the cognizance Virtues.

title: Cognizance
heading: Cognizance
summary: Describes how incognizant, narrowly cognizant and highly cognizant faeries differ in their understanding of advancement.
quotes: Only highly cognizant faeries understand that they can use human vitality and creativity to tailor their roles in amusing ways.

title: Vitality
heading: Vitality
summary: Faeries store Pretense points as vitality for changing role, and can consume encased vis to lower the cost of change.
quotes: it reduces the Pretence Cost in the nearby table by 1 for every pawn of vis consumed, to a maximum of the faerie's Might score

title: Using Abilities On Faeries
heading: Using Abilities On Faeries
summary: Summarises how the common Abilities (Animal Handling, Animal Ken, Folk Ken, Faerie Lore, Language, Teaching and social Abilities) apply to faeries.
quotes: Any Faerie with a score in Faerie Speech can understand any language.
Faeries cannot be taught, since they do not learn by doing.

title: Creativity
heading: Creativity
summary: Procedure and table by which a creative human collaborates to change a faerie's glamour, with Ease Factors, Pretense costs and the Virtue and Flaw changes they buy.
quotes: Lose a Virtue or Flaw and gain another of equal value
The Ease Factor should be reduced by 3 if the faerie’s role has drifted away from the folklore of the area

title: Why Isn't My Faerie a Genius At Every Ability?
heading: Why Isn't My Faerie a Genius At Every Ability?
summary: Explains why starting faerie characters lack great experience, including how and when faeries lose Pretenses.
quotes: Faeries often lose Pretenses.

title: Giants in Combat
heading: Giants in Combat
summary: Optional rules for fights between humans and giants: a defensive bonus for giants against scuffling, grappling and disarming, bending over, and the limits of Corpus spells on giants.
quotes: grant the giant a special defensive bonus equal to double the difference between its Size and a smaller opponent's
Giants of Size +4 or larger must bend over double in order to reach a Size 0 human with their hands.

title: Faerie Monarchs
heading: Faerie Monarchs
summary: Design benchmark for how mighty a faerie ruler must be to threaten senior magi and why a court helps.
quotes: it requires a Faerie Might score of around 60, and the Penetration Pretense

title: Sympathy
heading: Sympathy
requires: Sympathy Trait (from a Virtue or Faerie Warping)
summary: Introduces sympathy, the lingering connection to what a faerie represents that lets characters work Faerie hedge wizardry; it is not an Arcane Connection.
quotes: Sympathy represents a mystic relationship with a type of subject through the Faerie realm.

title: Sympathy Traits
heading: Sympathy Traits
requires: Sympathy Trait (from a Virtue or Faerie Warping)
summary: Defines Sympathy Traits, which can act as a specialization bonus on non-Supernatural Abilities, and negative Traits that penalise Abilities and add botch dice.
quotes: you may add the value of the Sympathy Trait to the Ability instead of the +1 bonus for an applicable specialization
Negative Sympathy Traits also give the player a number of additional botch dice equal to the character's worst Trait on all botch rolls

title: Increasing Sympathy Traits
heading: Increasing Sympathy Traits
requires: Sympathy Trait (from a Virtue or Faerie Warping)
summary: How Sympathy Traits grow with experience (limited by Warping Score), fluctuate on stress die results, and can be adjusted as story rewards.
quotes: Practicing a Sympathy Trait for a season yields 5 experience points towards that Trait.
so long as the value of the Trait does not exceed the character's Warping Score

title: Faerie Rank
heading: Faerie Rank
requires: Sympathy Trait (from a Virtue or Faerie Warping)
summary: Faerie Rank measures a character's overall connection to Faerie from the best positive and worst negative Sympathy Traits, and affects how faeries regard the character.
quotes: It is the value of the character's highest positive Sympathy Trait, modified by the character's lowest negative Sympathy Trait.

title: Sympathetic Influence Table
heading: Sympathetic Influence
requires: Sympathy Trait (from a Virtue or Faerie Warping)
summary: Table converting a sympathetic influence roll into the Sympathy Trait value gained.
quotes: +3 or –3 (max)

title: Sympathetic Influence
heading: Sympathetic Influence
requires: Sympathy Trait (from a Virtue or Faerie Warping)
summary: Procedure for temporarily gaining a Sympathy Trait by ceremonial or practical influence, using a Leadership roll tied to an appropriate Personality Trait.
quotes: a simple die + Presence + Leadership
Sympathy Traits gained through sympathetic influence cannot be increased with experience points

title: Tinted Auras
heading: Tinted Auras
requires: Sympathy Trait (from a Virtue or Faerie Warping)
summary: Rules for tinting a Faerie aura so that everyone within gains temporary Personality Traits, including the roll, how long tints last and combining tints.
quotes: stress die + Presence + Concentration
In a tinted aura, every character is strangely drawn to things that are associated with the tint, and repelled by things that are not.

title: Tinting an Aura Table
heading: Tinting an Aura
requires: Sympathy Trait (from a Virtue or Faerie Warping)
summary: Table of Ease Factors for tinting a Faerie aura to a given Personality Trait value.

title: Charms
heading: Charms
summary: Explains how a Virtue can be tied to a secret faerie charm through the Charm Flaws, how the charm is lost if shared, and which Virtues may be charmed.
quotes: The Virtue must affect what the character can do, not who he is.
if other characters become party to the charm, the power vanishes like mist in the sunlight

title: Folk Charms
heading: Folk Charms
summary: Hedge-magic charm that ends a faerie effect, rolled with Intelligence and Faerie Lore, at the cost of a Fatigue level and a Warping point.
quotes: stress die + Intelligence + Faerie Lore + aura
Activating a folk charm costs a Fatigue level and gives the character a point of Warping.

title: Hermetic Charms
heading: Hermetic Charms
requires: Sympathy Trait gained from exposure to the Faerie realm
summary: Lets a magus apply Sympathy Traits to Hermetic Abilities, Lab Totals, talisman attunement and charmed devices, and treat the work as a Magic or Faerie effect for Realm Interaction.
quotes: Sympathy Traits can be used as specializations to boost Abilities used to perform Hermetic magic, including Penetration and Magic Theory.
he may add the value of any of his Sympathy Traits that are appropriate to the shape or material to his Lab Total

title: Examples of Charmed Virtues
heading: Examples of Charmed Virtues
summary: Sidebar giving example Virtues with the charm that activates each.
